prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Document summary (≤500 words, ideology-neutral, no names)

The document outlines a five-year programme focused on economic policy, public services, constitutional arrangements, security, and digital change.

Economy and business
- Maintain fiscal discipline with a balanced budget targeted by the middle of the next decade; keep taxes low, raise the personal allowance to £12,500 and the higher-rate threshold to £50,000 by 2020; no VAT increase.
- Cut Corporation Tax to 17% by 2020; reform business rates (more frequent revaluations, possible self-assessment, full system review).
- Pursue free trade: a new UK trade policy, replication of existing EU deals where possible, Trade Commissioners network, reconvened Board of Trade, strengthened UK Export Finance.
- Tighten corporate governance: binding annual shareholder votes on executive pay, publish pay ratios, strengthen takeover scrutiny, protect critical infrastructure.
- Enhance worker protections (including for platform work) and raise the National Living Wage to 60% of median earnings by 2020.
- Industrial strategy: increase R&D to 2.4% of GDP within 10 years (3% longer term), expand university investment funds, create “Future Britain” sovereign-style funds, support key sectors (advanced manufacturing, life sciences, creative, digital), and back small businesses via procurement targets and prompt payment.
- Energy: independent review of costs, industrial energy efficiency scheme, diverse generation (offshore wind leadership; onshore wind not expanded in England; support island wind in Scotland); develop shale with a new regulator and community benefit fund.
- Infrastructure: HS2, Northern rail, Heathrow expansion; road upgrades; £600m for ultra-low-emission vehicles; expand cycling.

Regions, rural and coastal
- Devolution within the UK maintained and potentially expanded post‑EU exit; Shared Prosperity Fund to replace EU structural funds.
- Move civil service and cultural bodies out of London; relocate a public broadcaster.
- Rural: maintain farm support cash totals to 2022; new agri‑environment system next parliament; animal welfare measures; expand post office banking; support Welsh-language broadcasting.
- Coastal: extend Coastal Communities Fund; new fisheries policy outside the Common Fisheries Policy.

EU exit and constitution
- Seek a “deep and special” partnership with the EU; leave the single market and customs union; Great Repeal Bill to convert EU law; protect workers’ rights at exit; parliamentary vote on final deal.
- Electoral and constitutional changes: voter ID, boundary review to 600 MPs, repeal Fixed-term Parliaments Act, retain first-past-the-post for more elections.

Security, justice, defence, and aid
- Maintain defence spending at least 2% of GDP and increase by ≥0.5% above inflation annually; sustain nuclear deterrent; major equipment investment; enhanced veterans’ support.
- Create a national infrastructure police force; fold the Serious Fraud Office into the National Crime Agency; bolster cyber security.
- Justice reforms: victim entitlements in law, prison modernisation with 10,000 places, stronger community sentencing; tackle hate crime.

Public services and society
- NHS: at least £8bn real-terms increase over five years; expand training places; invest in estates and technology; faster access to new treatments; seven‑day services; 10,000 more mental health staff; improved cancer standards.
- Social care: include home value in means-testing for home and residential care; a £100,000 asset floor; universal deferral so no home sale in lifetime; means-test Winter Fuel Payments; new carer’s leave.
- Education: fund schools with an extra £4bn by 2022; continue free schools; allow new selective schools with conditions; expand maths schools; revise faith school rules; EBacc targets; replace universal infant lunches with universal free breakfasts; protect Pupil Premium.
- Technical skills: introduce T‑levels, expand apprenticeships, create institutes of technology; national retraining scheme; discounted travel for apprentices.
- Housing: deliver 1.5m homes by 2022; council housing deals with fixed-term social homes and a linked Right to Buy; protect Green Belt; crack down on unfair leaseholds; reform homebuying; tenant security.
- Cost of living and consumer markets: stronger regulators, energy safeguard tariff cap and smart meters, fairer telecoms billing, rail ticketing reform, minimum service levels in rail strikes, debt “Breathing Space.”
- Migration: reduce net migration to sustainable levels; tighter student and family visas; new EU migration system post‑exit; integration and counter‑extremism measures.
- Inequalities and protection: actions on gender and ethnicity pay gaps, disability employment, domestic abuse bill, halve rough sleeping by 2022 and end by 2027.

Digital
- Digital Charter: stronger data protection law, right to delete youth data at 18, online harms levy and sanctions, obligations on platforms.
- Infrastructure: broadband universal service by 2020; fibre and 5G rollout; expand mobile coverage to 95% of UK geography by 2022.
- Digital government: Verify rollout, open data expansion, geospatial data body; maintain media freedom framework (no Leveson 2; repeal Section 40).
